items.title: Tatva Chintan Q2 FY27 profit up 116% to ₹21.5 crore; five semiconductor products still in qualification
items.text: Tatva Chintan reported Q2 FY27 revenue from operations of ₹217.3 crore, up 76% from ₹123.5 crore, with EBITDA excluding other income of ₹40.7 crore (19% margin) and consolidated net profit of ₹21.5 crore versus ₹9.9 crore (results disclosed in filings dated 19 Oct 2026). The stock traded at ₹2,026.40 at 9:15 AM on 21 Oct, up 7% from the previous close. The company said its five semiconductor chemical products remain at different stages of development, validation and customer qualification, and no segment revenue was given, so semiconductor sales are not yet a visible driver of earnings.

items.title: India targets $1 trillion chemicals industry by 2040, with semiconductor chemicals a priority area
items.text: Chemical Industry Digest, citing breakthroughgroup.com, reports India aims for a $1 trillion chemicals industry by 2040, with semiconductor chemicals one of three priority areas alongside specialty chemicals and battery materials. The government is pursuing it through infrastructure, targeted R&D incentives and sector-specific policies, and the article says FDI and international technology partners could help. No semiconductor-specific figures or new scheme details are given, so this is a policy signal rather than a funded measure.

sources.title: India Sets 2040 Ambition for Global Leadership in Technology and Specialty Chemicals

items.title: Supreme Court stays coercive action against Tata Chemicals in Gulf of Kutch case
items.text: On 5 Oct 2026 the Supreme Court directed that no coercive action be taken against Tata Chemicals over alleged damage to the Gulf of Kutch Marine Sanctuary, which a Gujarat High Court ruling had held it liable for. The Gujarat Pollution Control Board is to assess the damage and remediation cost within three months. Shares rose 2.16% to ₹620.90 on the NSE. This is not semiconductor-specific, but it removes near-term overhang for a listed name on the page.

items.title: Linde India secures 8-acre Sanand plot for semiconductor packaging gas facility
items.text: Linde India has acquired about 8 acres in Sanand, Gujarat for a gas facility serving semiconductor packaging units, and says it is in talks with potential customers on long-term supply contracts. Micron, CG Power and Kaynes Technology have packaging and testing projects in Sanand. It complements the air separation unit under development in Dholera for Tata Electronics' fab. Price and commissioning date were not disclosed; the shares stood at ₹6,189 on 28 Sep, up 0.76%.
